author: OPUS-PEOPLE (research helper, read-only web research)
use: Checks for M1-11: how often a job loss, eviction or closure turns into a cause, a grudge or a new ambition. Rates check totals; they never pick one person's outcome. Figures marked secondary must be checked against the paper before they tune a parameter.

participation.finding: One involuntary job loss in prime working years: about 35% lower odds of joining community groups decades later (odds ratio about 0.68).
Early-adult unemployment slows the growth of political interest; no effect later in life; strongest for introverts.
participation.citation: Emmenegger, Marx and Schraff 2017, Journal of Politics 79(1)

participation.finding: A 2-point rise in state unemployment raises turnout about 1 point, while the unemployed still vote less than the employed.
participation.citation: Burden and Wichowsky 2014, Journal of Politics 76(4):887-898

grievance.finding: Job loss raises support for welfare spending by 22-25 points, fading on reemployment: a policy shift more than a lasting grudge.
No representative rate of lasting blame of the employer exists; one nonrepresentative survey had 71% blaming company leadership.

ambition.finding: Working at a firm that goes bankrupt adds 3.7 points for men and 1.8 for women to becoming an entrepreneur within 4 years (baselines about 2.4% and 1%).
ambition.citation: Roed and Skogstrom 2014, Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 76(5):727-744, doi:10.1111/obes.12042

ambition.finding: Plant-closure displacement roughly doubles self-employment entry the next year.
About 16% of displaced workers completed community-college credit (men under 35 16.8%, 35+ 10.9%; women under 35 23.5%, 35+ 17.2%).
ambition.citation: Jacobson, LaLonde and Sullivan 2005, Journal of Econometrics (Chicago Fed WP 2003-25)

ambition.finding: About 10% of displaced workers enroll in public college; about 1 in 100 because of the displacement.
ambition.citation: Minaya, Moore and Scott-Clayton 2020, NBER w27694

ambition.finding: Job loss raises joining a party and running for local council (Brazil).

carryOn.finding: Effects of economic shocks on politics are real but small and often transient; 65% of workers displaced 2019-21 were reemployed by January 2022.
carryOn.citation: Margalit 2019, Annual Review of Political Science 22; BLS Displaced Worker Supplement 2022

participation.finding: A 1-point rise in a neighborhood's eviction rate lowers turnout about 2.7 points (neighborhood level; no individual rate).
participation.citation: Slee and Desmond 2023, Politics and Society 51(1):3-29, doi:10.1177/00323292211050716

grievance.finding: Nearly all evicted tenants attribute the eviction to the landlord (qualitative); no representative rate of lasting anger.
About 50% of evicted mothers reported depression against 25% of matched mothers, hardship elevated two years later.

ambition.finding: Of 2,607 failed entrepreneurs in 23 countries, 24% were already starting again and 16% intended to; about 60% showed no reentry.
ambition.citation: Simmons, Wiklund and Levie 2014, Small Business Economics 42(3):485-505

grievance.finding: Reviews grief, self-blame and blame of outside causes; no population rates.
grievance.citation: Ucbasaran et al. 2013, Journal of Management 39(1):163-202, doi:10.1177/0149206312457823

employeeOfClosedBusiness: Treated as plant-closure displacement: the job-loss rows apply.
